context: seed: the budgets of this world sit at the knowing policy's calls or one above them (suite/families/curriculum.py:111 and the SLACK table); the shell tool refuses a call past its budget (suite/tools.py:87) and the HTTP tool likewise (suite/tools.py:70)
counterfactual: The overshoot is one call per input, or a look before the answer — suite/families/genesis.py:48 spends five calls against a budget of two — and the refusal is suite/tools.py:87 on the shell and suite/tools.py:70 on the HTTP tool; the other overshoot is batching calls whose later inputs an earlier call must supply.
decision: Under a call budget, plan every call before the first one and spend none on discovery the store has already settled: no `ls`, `cat`, `head` or `wc` to look at a file before the command that computes the answer, and no probing call before the one the convention names. Independent inputs (several named files) go into one command; a chain the world dictates (each page's `next`) is one call per link. The knowing count is the floor: one shell call for a line total, a CSV count or a CSV sum; one HTTP call for a resource, a status or a secure route; one call per page for a listing. A call spent looking is the call the budget does not hold.

residue: whether inputs are truly independent is judgment

not_this: a task with no budget on the tool it uses
a call whose input the world can only supply through an earlier call — a page's next path, a 410's successor — which is a link of the walk, not discovery
an output-schema task that makes no tool call

lifecycle.consumer: the working pass, at boot, on a matching work-shape
lifecycle.moot_when: no tool runs under a budget
